I do not have a proof or a complete feasible counterexample to the unrestricted allocation
$$2G+B_U+B_R\le 2N+2B_{11}+\Lambda.$$
I obtained a new, general single-use injection into your exact defects, and a conditional construction that resolves all support-completion obligations for a substantial counterexample route. Neither result settles the full target.The new injection handles every occupied U11 tip gate whose cap-to-tip chain has a nonfull receiver, jointly with positive legs whose exterior supports are consumed. Its payments cannot overlap. The remaining cases are U01 upper-corner gates and U11 tip gates with completely full cap-to-tip chains.Throughout, I use your established catalogue, original-owner event ledger, marked-side assignment, canonical-tile distinctness, and exact identity
$$R:=S+C-K_{\mathrm{irregular}},\qquad
2R=A_++G_b+U_0+Z_0+E.
\tag{1}$$
1. A new universal single-use chain allocationCall a physical tile full when all four corners belong to final  $P$ .Define two actual geometric counts. $H_{\mathrm{break}}$  counts occupied canonical positive gates owned by a phase- $(1,1)$  terminal tip for which that foreign leg has either an unfilled original triple cap or a nonfull original regular receiver somewhere between the cap and its tip. $L_{\mathrm{ext}}$  counts positive-U legs having either a consumed original selection in one of their regular  $2P1T$  receivers or an activated terminal  $1P2T$  singleton. Count each leg once. In particular,  $L_{\mathrm{ext}}\ge A_+$ .Then, for the complete fixed-source model with all the dimensions and phases in the question,
$$\boxed{
H_{\mathrm{break}}+L_{\mathrm{ext}}
\le U_0+A_++E.
}
\tag{2}$$
Consequently,
$$\boxed{
2R\ge G_b+Z_0+H_{\mathrm{break}}+L_{\mathrm{ext}}.
}
\tag{3}$$
This is a joint injection into actual defects. It does not assign another payment from  $C$ , and it does not use a filled  $3+1$  tile as a fresh payment.The common stopping tileBoth families of chains stop at the same configuration: an original regular  $2P1T$  receiver whose selection has become a foreign original endpoint, while its old blank corner remains nonendpoint.Write its original pair as  $p,q$ , its selection as  $t$ , and its blank as  $b$ , with  $t$  adjacent to  $p,b$ . At a nonfull stop,
$$p,q,t\in P,\qquad b\notin P.$$
The corner  $b$  cannot be retained selected, since it sees both  $q$  and  $t$ . It is finally blank.Consider the original owner of  $t$ . The point  $b$  was originally blank for that owner. Since  $t$  originally had occupied degree three, its other intratile neighbor  $p$  was originally occupied. Endpoint disjointness excludes  $p$  from that owner’s original endpoint set, so  $p$  was its selection.Thus  $t$  is an original irregular  $1P1T$  singleton. Its unique blank is  $b$ , which remains blank, so it does not fire. The original regular pair does not fire either. Therefore
$$i_Q=1,\qquad
k_Q=c_Q=b_Q=d_Q=f_Q=0,
\qquad
\Lambda_Q=1.
\tag{4}$$
Once  $g_Q=0$  is checked, this gives exactly
$$E_Q=1.
\tag{5}$$
The ownership in this argument remains original throughout. In particular, neither endpoint of the regular pair is reclassified, and the pair need not be an original matching edge.Positive exterior chainsNormalize a positive U to  $U(w,a,b)$ . Its left regular receivers, including the bar-end receiver, are
$$Q_j=\{2j,2j+1\}\times\{0,1\},
\qquad 0\le j<a/2,$$
with original data
$$P_i\cap Q_j=\{(2j,1),(2j+1,1)\},\quad
t_j=(2j,0),\quad b_j=(2j+1,0).
\tag{6}$$
If the terminal singleton is already activated, assign this leg to its own  $A_+$  occurrence.Otherwise, start at a consumed  $t_j$ , choosing the first such receiver from the bar.If  $Q_j$  is nonfull, it is the stopping configuration above. If it is full, then  $b_j\in P$ . The next mandatory selection
$$t_{j+1}=(2j+2,0)$$
sees its persistent original anchor  $(2j+2,1)$  and  $b_j$ . It therefore must be an original foreign endpoint. Continue down the leg.Fullness of the last regular receiver forces the terminal selection  $(a,0)$  to be consumed, activating the tip. Thus every counted positive leg obtains either its own activated terminal occurrence or a first nonfull stopping tile.At such a stopping tile,  $g_Q=0$ . A blank-gate mark requires an assigned original U11 upper corner or terminal tip in that tile. The old pair belongs to a positive source. The only foreign endpoint is the irregular singleton from (4), and U11 has no irregular singleton profile. None of the three endpoints can supply the required blank-gate assignment.Hence the stop supplies an actual  $E_Q=1$  unit.Reflection proves the right-leg assertion. Independent leg heights and all effective-positive isometries are covered by transporting these coordinates.U11 cap-to-tip chainsNormalize the foreign U11 owner as  $U(w,a,b)+(1,1)$ . Its left triple cap is
$$Q_{\mathrm{cap}}=\{2,3\}\times\{2,3\},$$
with original endpoints
$$(2,2),(2,3),(3,2)$$
and missing corner  $m=(3,3)$ .Its regular cap-to-tip receivers are

\qquad 2\le j\le a/2,$$
with

t_j=(2j,3),\quad b_j=(2j+1,3).

For a gate counted by  $H_{\mathrm{break}}$ , an unfilled cap supplies its own  $U_0$  unit.If the cap is full,  $m\in P$ . Then  $t_2=(4,3)$  sees both  $m$  and its original anchor  $(4,2)$ , so it must be consumed. Fullness of  $Q_j$  similarly forces consumption of  $t_{j+1}$ .Because this chain is counted by  $H_{\mathrm{break}}$ , a first nonfull regular receiver exists when the cap is full. It supplies the configuration in (4).Again  $g_Q=0$ :At an interior stop, neither old endpoint is a U11 upper corner or terminal tip; the foreign irregular singleton cannot be one either.At a terminal stop, the physical tile is already the original canonical tile of the occupied positive gate being routed. Distinctness of all original canonical positive tiles excludes another blank-gate side there, and the gate of the side being routed is occupied.Thus every such stop supplies one  $E_Q=1$  unit.Why the payments are jointly distinctThe injectivity covers both families together.Every stopping tile contains the routed leg’s original endpoint pair and exactly one foreign endpoint. Two different routes have disjoint original pairs. If they stopped at the same tile, that tile would contain four endpoints and would be full. Therefore no stopping  $E_Q$  unit is used twice.Each U11 leg has one associated triple cap. Its terminal tip can own at most one canonical positive gate, by canonical-tile distinctness. Hence no  $U_0$  occurrence is assigned twice. An unfilled triple cap also cannot coincide with a stop for a different original pair: the disjoint triple and pair would require five corners.Each positive terminal activation belongs to one original positive leg, which is counted once. These are source-owned  $A_+$  occurrences, exactly as in (1).This proves (2), and substitution into (1) proves (3). The alternating mandatory supports are essential to the propagation; no support is discarded.2. The zero-reserve obstruction is now more rigidFor  $N=1$ , a violation of the requested allocation must have
$$G=2,\qquad R=0.
\tag{8}$$
Equation (1) then forces
$$A_+=G_b=U_0=Z_0=E=0.
\tag{9}$$
The complete support obligations give three structural consequences.Every positive receiver keeps its original profileBy (2),  $R=0$  implies  $L_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$ . No positive regular receiver selection is consumed, and no positive terminal singleton is activated.An old blank in a regular  $2P1T$  receiver cannot become a foreign endpoint without forcing that receiver full and consuming its selection. Additions of retained foreign selections at such blanks are excluded by persistent anchors. At a terminal  $1P2T$  receiver, occupation of its remaining diagonal corner would also force activation of its selections.Consequently, every original receiver tile of every positive U has exactly its original final profile. Consumption of inward supports outside those receiver tiles remains possible.This distinction matters: a saturated counterexample would have to destroy the inner canonical donors while preserving the entire exterior receiver strip and both tip receivers.Every U11 receiver is fullAn original U11  $2P0T$  bar receiver cannot remain nonfull when  $E=G_b=0$ . If unchanged, it leaves positive defect; if enlarged to a nonfull mixed three-endpoint tile, it leaves one defect unit.Both original triple caps are full because  $U_0=0$ . From each full cap, the propagation in (7) consumes the next mandatory inward selection. A first nonfull receiver would contribute  $E_Q=1$ , since  $G_b=0$ . Hence the propagation fills the entire leg, including its terminal receiver.The catalogue therefore gives
$$\boxed{\text{Every original U11 receiver is full when }R=0.}
\tag{10}$$
A firing U01 tip fills its inward chain back to its geometric gateNormalize a U01 left tip as
$$p=(a,2),\qquad \delta(p)=(a,3).$$
If it fires,  $(a,3)\in P$ . The preceding endpoint  $(a-1,2)$  has the mandatory inward support
$$x=(a-1,3).$$
This support sees its original anchor and the endpoint  $(a,3)$ , so it must be consumed.Its original regular receiver must then be full under  $R=0$ . Its newly filled inward corner forces the next inward support above it to be consumed. Repetition reaches
$$\{2,3\}\times\{2,3\},$$
whose original blank is the source’s same-leg geometric gate  $(2,3)$ . That receiver is full.This statement applies to the firing tip’s owner. It does not automatically fill the receiving, nonfiring owner’s leg.Combining these consequences with the occupied-gate catalogue, any  $N=1,R=0,G=2$  violation would have both canonical tiles full. Its occupied gates could only be U01 upper corners or U11 terminal tips on completely full chains. A U10 gate would activate a positive tip, contradicting (9).These are necessary conditions, not an impossibility proof.3. Then

\tag{13}$$
Every positive core canonical gate lies in  $I$ , and both outer canonical gates lie in  $C$ .Both terminal selections of every positive core singleton are consumed, while the outer positive tips remain unactivated. Hence
$$A_+=2k.$$
All core and frame receiver tiles are full. Therefore

The exact defect identity gives

It follows that
$$\boxed{N+R-G=-1,}
\tag{14}$$
or, in the question’s doubled allocation,
$$\boxed{
2G-\bigl(2N+A_++G_b+U_0+Z_0+E\bigr)=2.
}
\tag{15}$$
The actual ambient coefficient-one inequality still holds in this construction. In the even rectangle

|T|=r+14,$$
so
$$\boxed{\sigma=2q+1>0.}

No endpoint rectangle tiling has been supplied here. Therefore this is a conditional construction, not a counterexample. What is proved is the implication
$$\boxed{
\text{A rectangle tiled by permitted original endpoint shapes}
\Longrightarrow
\text{a complete feasible violation of the joint allocation}.
}
\tag{17}$$
Thus a universal proof of the requested allocation would also prove that this entire endpoint-shape family cannot tile any rectangle. The remaining mathematical gapThe new injection removes two sources of ambiguity:A U11 occupied tip gate whose chain is not entirely full has a distinct payment in  $U_0$  or  $E$ .Consumption of positive exterior receiver supports has a distinct payment in  $A_+$  or  $E$ , jointly with the first family.The payments use unfilled caps, nonfull stopping tiles, and original positive activation occurrences. They never charge a filled  $3+1$  contact again.What remains is a finite, source-dependent count through U01 upper-corner contacts and completely full U11 cap-to-tip chains. In a completely full chain there need be no  $U_0$  or  $E$  at which to stop. Its physical full-tile credit has already entered the exact local accounting, so fullness alone supplies no additional payment. The rotor-only rectangle Euler argument also needs a justified adapter across these U caps before it can count such a mixed component.The proved chain allocation and saturation lemmas constrain that missing adapter, while the rectangle construction identifies a concrete global packing obstruction it would have to overcome. They do not yet establish
$$G\le N+R,$$
and I have not produced a complete feasible fusion violating it.
